newsitem.title: UK: Euro sour crude crumples under fresh Iraqi volumes.
newsitem.headline: Euro sour crude crumples under fresh Iraqi volumes.

text.p: European sour crude markets have weakened under pressure from fresh Iraqi spot volumes and plentiful supplies of other sour grades, oil traders said on Friday.
Iraq's State Oil Marketing Organisation (SOMO) is touting extra spot volumes to make up for a shortfall in revenue from the U.N. oil-for food plan caused by falling world oil prices.
Traders estimate that this could add a further two million barrels to the 9.4 million barrel February loading programme for Kirkuk crude at the Turkish Mediterranean port of Ceyhan.
A crude trader for Mineralimpex, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Hungarian refiner MOL, confirmed on Friday that it had a spot deal with SOMO for a one million barrel cargo.
A crude buyer for the refiner said the sale had already won U.N. approval, but would not comment on whether further deals were expected.
The trader said that the cargo would be lifted before March 9, the end of the first 90 period of Iraqi sales.
Under the terms of the deal, Iraq is permitted to sell $1 billion worth of crude during the first 90 day period, and then another $1 billion over the next 90 days.

But because of a 14 percent fall in world oil prices since the beginning of January, U.N. overseers put the total value of the first three month's worth of sales contracts at $800-million, and are expected to sanction Iraqi spot sales to make up the shortfall in revenue.
Other European oil traders also reported being offered Iraqi spot volumes.
"There are definitely extra avails on offer," said a trader at a West European oil company which has a term contract to lift Iraqi crude under the U.N. deal.
But traders said that SOMO was likely to have difficulty moving extra volumes in a well-supplied sour market.

Prices for Russian Urals, the region's sour crude marker, have slid to Dated Brent -90/-80 cents with some dealers expecting it to drop under the $1 mark next week with a heavy loading programme scheduled at the main Black Sea outlet of Novorossiisk.
"There's lots of Urals due to load next week. If Novo is open I see it going below (Dated Brent -$1)," said one.
Two Syrian Light cargoes were also seen still on offer in the Mediterranean, dealers said.
Plentiful supplies of other grades and weak refining margins should push Kirkuk prices below the Dated Brent -$1.55 a barrel level fixed for European buyers for the first contract period.
"Dated Brent -$1.55 was fixed (for Kirkuk) when Urals was up as high as Dated -20 or 30," said one trader. "They'd have to drop the prices," said one Mediterranean trader.
